supplement_gap_material.auxiliary_material: The study highlights regimen-specific effects, noting that microbial associations with outcomes differed between the PD-1 inhibitor-based regimen (PC) and the dual checkpoint blockade regimen (NIC). It identifies specific bacterial genera (Fusicatenibacter, Butyricicoccus, Blautia) enriched in patients with longer OS (>12 or >18 months). It also notes that lower microbial alpha diversity and presence of certain taxa were linked to a higher risk of serious (≥ Grade 4) AEs. The authors conclude that gut microbiota may serve as a biomarker for chemo-immunotherapy in advanced NSCLC.
supplement_gap_material.outline_action: No further action required; the gap is fulfilled by the existence of the JCOG2007 phase III RCT described in this study.
supplement_gap_material.useful_material: This study reports on the JCOG2007 trial, a completed phase III randomized controlled trial comparing pembrolizumab plus platinum doublet chemotherapy (PC) and nivolumab-ipilimumab plus platinum doublet chemotherapy (NIC) in treatment-naïve advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients. The trial enrolled 295 patients, with an ancillary biomarker analysis performed on baseline fecal samples from 270 patients using 16S rDNA sequencing. The study found that gut microbiota composition was associated with overall survival (OS) and adverse events (AEs). Specifically, higher abundance of Fusicatenibacter and Butyricicoccus was linked to better OS in the NIC arm compared to the PC arm, and these genera were also associated with a lower risk of serious AEs. Conversely, higher abundance of Prevotellaceae NK3B31 was associated with higher mortality risk in the NIC arm.
